target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∃ (D Ic Rc E : Type) (u1 : D → Ic) (u2 : D → Rc) (c2 : Ic → Set E) (c4 : Rc → E)
    (Y V2 : Set D),
    Y ⊆ V2 ∧ (∃ f : Rc → Ic, ∀ o ∈ V2, u1 o = f (u2 o)) ∧
    (¬ ∃ o ∈ Y, c4 (u2 o) ∉ c2 (u1 o)) ∧ (∃ o ∈ V2, c4 (u2 o) ∉ c2 (u1 o))
translation: Target is defined as a proposition (it is named, not asserted or proved) that does not reference any of the preceding definitions. It states that there exist four types D, Ic, Rc, and E, four functions u1 : D → Ic, u2 : D → Rc, c2 : Ic → Set E (mapping each element of Ic to a set of elements of E), and c4 : Rc → E, and two subsets Y and V2 of D, such that all four of the following conditions hold simultaneously: (1) Y is a subset of V2; (2) there exists a function f : Rc → Ic such that for every o in V2, u1 o = f (u2 o) (this equality is only required on V2, not on all of D); (3) there does not exist an o in Y such that c4 (u2 o) is not in c2 (u1 o) (equivalently, classically, for every o in Y, c4 (u2 o) ∈ c2 (u1 o)); and (4) there exists an o in V2 such that c4 (u2 o) is not in c2 (u1 o). No further conditions are placed on the types, functions, or sets—for instance, Y is not required to be nonempty, and the types and functions are completely unconstrained beyond the four clauses above.

divergences.description: Because Target is an existential statement with no nondegeneracy constraints on Y (the datasets O that can arise) or on c2 (the predicted experience sets), it can be witnessed trivially by setting Y = ∅, V2 = {()} (making strict dependence vacuous on a singleton), and c2 _ = ∅ (making no predictions at all). Although nontrivial witnesses with nonempty Y and nonempty predictions also exist, the formal statement itself does not rule out a degenerate witness.

Target uses a standalone simplified model of a theory of consciousness without the physical-system layer (P, c1) of S3, takes inference c4 : Rc → E to be single-valued (defining falsification as c4 (u2 o) ∉ c2 (u1 o)), and leaves V2 unconstrained beyond Y ⊆ V2 (omitting both the inference-content and prediction-content pairing restrictions from the proof of Theorem 4.3, though the author's claim explicitly disclaims representing Kleiner and Hoel's intended reading of O̅).

judgement.summary: Target faithfully formalizes the author's counterexample claim—existence of a setup with O ⊆ O̅, strict dependence oi = f(or) on O̅ (Definition 4.2), no falsification on O, and a falsification on O̅ (negating empirical unfalsifiability per Definition 4.1)—with only minor caveats regarding missing nondegeneracy conditions (such as Y being nonempty) and the simplified standalone model of prediction and inference.
